title: DDD entities value objects aggregates and bounded contexts
concepts: Domain-driven design is a collaborative modeling approach: strategic design aligns software boundaries with domain language, while tactical patterns express domain rules inside a model.
A bounded context defines where a model and its ubiquitous language have a specific meaning; the same real-world identity may be represented differently in another context.
An entity is defined by identity and continuity; a value object is defined by its values and is commonly immutable; the choice depends on domain meaning, not database shape.
An aggregate is a transactional consistency boundary with exactly one root that protects its invariants; aggregate boundaries should follow business transactions rather than object graphs.
Domain services express domain rules that do not naturally belong to one entity or value object; application services orchestrate a use case without taking ownership of domain rules.
Domain events describe meaningful changes inside a model; integration events communicate across bounded contexts after the originating change is committed.
DDD is a modeling toolkit, not a mandate to use microservices, rich object models, or every named pattern in every application.
